PWA prompt heading correctly reads 'Install efoodtech' — verified in source AND rendered card (synthetic beforeinstallprompt dispatched, screenshot captured). Admin end-to-end login with phone 9175560211 works: fresh session -> verify-otp -> hard nav to /admin -> AdminLayout with full sidebar (dashboard/control-tower/plans/users-roles/etc.) rendered, header shows 'efoodtech'. Footer rebrand DID NOT land — GET /api/content/footer still returns brand_name='efoodcare', copyright='copyright © efoodcare.in all rights reserved', promise mentions efoodcare. Root cause identified: /app/backend/server.py DEFAULT_CONTENT['footer'] (lines 1503-1518) has DUPLICATE keys — 'brand_name' is set to 'efoodtech' on line 1506 then re-assigned to 'efoodcare' on line 1513; 'promise' is similarly re-assigned to the efoodcare copy on line 1514. Python dict literal keeps only the last assignment, so defaults resolve to efoodcare. Additionally the site_content DB doc may hold a stale override that shadows even a corrected default.

rca of the issue: Python dict literal duplicate-key silent overwrite. In /app/backend/server.py the DEFAULT_CONTENT['footer'] dict literal declares brand_name twice (L1506 'efoodtech', L1513 'efoodcare') and promise twice (L1508 efoodtech copy, L1514 efoodcare copy). Python evaluates the literal by inserting each key in order, so the FIRST value is discarded and the SECOND (efoodcare) wins. That's why the API returns efoodcare even though the iter-151 diff added the efoodtech values. Mitigation: (1) delete the duplicate 'brand_name'/'promise'/'website'/'email' entries from the second half of the literal, keeping only the efoodtech copies; (2) either drop the site_content doc for key='footer' in Mongo or call POST /api/admin/content/footer/reset after backend restart so no stale override survives; (3) add a ruff/flake8 F601 check to CI to catch dict duplicate keys in future rebrand PRs.
